items.q: Amyloid deposits are confirmed histologically by which finding?
o: Congo red with apple green birefringence
items.exp: Amyloid fibrils bind Congo red and show apple green birefringence under polarised light. This remains the defining histological confirmation before protein typing.
r: Incorrect. PAS stains glycogen and fungal walls, not amyloid specifically.
Correct. Apple green birefringence on Congo red confirms amyloid.
Incorrect. Prussian blue detects iron in haemochromatosis.
Incorrect. Oil red O detects neutral fat in frozen sections.
items.kp: Congo red plus apple green birefringence equals amyloid.

items.q: Nephrotic syndrome, restrictive cardiomyopathy, macroglossia and a plasma cell clone indicate which amyloid type?
items.exp: AL amyloid from clonal light chains causes this multisystem pattern including macroglossia. AA disease follows chronic inflammation and mainly affects kidney without a clone.
r: Incorrect. AA follows chronic inflammation without a clone or macroglossia.
Correct. Clone plus macroglossia means AL amyloid.
Incorrect. Transthyretin disease is mainly cardiac and nerve in older adults.
Incorrect. Dialysis amyloid affects joints after long dialysis.
items.kp: Clone plus big tongue plus stiff heart: AL amyloid.

items.q: AA amyloidosis is most likely to follow which condition?
items.exp: AA amyloid precursor serum amyloid A rises in chronic inflammation, so rheumatoid arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease and chronic suppuration are classic antecedents.
r: Incorrect. Myeloma associates with AL, not AA, amyloid.
Correct. Chronic rheumatoid inflammation drives AA amyloid.
Incorrect. Brief viral illness does not sustain precursor elevation.
Incorrect. Iron deficiency does not cause amyloidosis.
items.kp: AA equals chronic inflammation; AL equals clone.

items.q: An ECG showing low voltage with echocardiographic thick walls most suggests what?
items.exp: Infiltrative amyloid thickens walls with electrically inert protein, lowering voltage, whereas true myocyte hypertrophy raises voltage. This mismatch is a high yield discriminator.
r: Incorrect. Hypertension raises both thickness and voltage.
Correct. Low voltage with thick walls means infiltration.
Incorrect. Athlete heart shows voltage criteria for hypertrophy.
Incorrect. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy typically increases voltage.
items.kp: Voltage mass mismatch should trigger an amyloid workup.

items.q: Wild type transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis in an elderly man is often preceded by which condition?
items.exp: Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome commonly precedes wild type transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis by five to ten years because amyloid deposits in flexor retinaculum before the heart fails.
r: Correct. Carpal tunnel often comes years before cardiac disease.
Incorrect. Ulcer disease has no such link.
Incorrect. Childhood asthma is unrelated.
Incorrect. Urinary infection does not precede this amyloid.
items.kp: Old man, stiff heart, old carpal tunnel: think transthyretin.

items.q: Dialysis related amyloidosis is formed from which precursor protein?
items.exp: Beta 2 microglobulin accumulates when renal clearance and older dialysis membranes fail to remove it, depositing in joints and causing carpal tunnel and arthropathy.
r: Incorrect. Light chains form AL amyloid.
Correct. Beta 2 microglobulin forms dialysis amyloid.
Incorrect. Serum amyloid A forms AA amyloid.
Incorrect. Transthyretin forms cardiac predominant amyloid.
items.kp: Dialysis amyloid precursor is beta 2 microglobulin.

items.q: Which biopsy site is preferred first for confirming systemic amyloidosis with least risk?
items.exp: Abdominal fat pad aspiration or biopsy detects amyloid in most systemic cases with minimal risk. Organ biopsy follows when fat pad is negative but suspicion remains high.
r: Incorrect. Lung biopsy carries unnecessary risk first.
Correct. Fat pad sampling is the safe first test.
Incorrect. Brain biopsy is reserved for cerebral disease.
Incorrect. Muscle biopsy is not the routine first site.
items.kp: Start with fat pad, escalate only if negative.

items.q: The fibrils of amyloid share which structural configuration?
items.exp: All amyloid types share cross beta pleated sheet fibrils that bind Congo red. Precursors differ, but this shared structure explains common staining and protease resistance.
r: Incorrect. Alpha helices do not define amyloid.
Correct. Beta pleated sheets define amyloid fibrils.
Incorrect. Triple helix defines collagen.
Incorrect. Amyloid is ordered, not random aggregate.
items.kp: Different proteins, one structure: beta pleated sheet.

items.q: Familial Mediterranean fever predisposes to which amyloid type through recurrent inflammation?
items.exp: Recurrent serosal inflammation in familial Mediterranean fever sustains serum amyloid A elevation, causing AA amyloidosis mainly of kidney. Colchicine prevents attacks and amyloid progression.
r: Incorrect. AL needs a plasma cell clone.
Correct. Recurrent inflammation causes AA amyloid.
Incorrect. Hereditary transthyretin causes neuropathic cardiac disease.
Incorrect. Beta 2 type needs dialysis exposure.
items.kp: Prevent AA amyloid by stopping the inflammation.

items.q: Periorbital purpura after minor procedures in amyloidosis reflects what?
o: Vascular fragility from amyloid infiltration, mainly AL
items.exp: Amyloid infiltrates vessel walls making them fragile, producing pinch or post procedure periorbital purpura, especially in AL disease. Acquired factor X deficiency may coexist in AL cases.
r: Incorrect. Platelet counts are often preserved.
Correct. Infiltrated fragile vessels cause the purpura.
Incorrect. Vitamin K deficiency causes broader coagulopathy.
Incorrect. Haemophilia causes deep joint bleeding, not this sign.
items.kp: Raccoon eyes after minor trauma should suggest AL amyloid.
